gold_decisions.identity_explanation: Both identify the false claim that the radial derivative control establishes convexity or monotonicity along the segment; both distinguish it from the valid restricted-secant consequence.
gold_decisions.shared_mathematical_weakness: The positive radial inner-product inequality does not imply monotonicity of the directional derivative or convexity of the surrogate along the segment.

component_coverage.gold_component: False radial-convexity interpretation of the surrogate despite only a positive radial derivative/secan​t inequality being established.

gold_decisions.identity_explanation: Both identify the unsupported identification of the aggregate outlier-gradient norm with the minimum of its upper bounds, including the failure caused by cancellation and the absence of a positive lower bound.
gold_decisions.shared_mathematical_weakness: The available upper bounds on the aggregate outlier gradient do not imply equality with their minimum or the advertised positive lower bound; cancellation can make the aggregate arbitrarily small or zero.

component_coverage.gold_component: Unsupported equality/minimum identification and failure of the positive aggregate outlier-gradient lower bound due to cancellation.

gold_decisions.identity_explanation: The prediction recognizes the substantive clean-curvature problem: the positive clean secant constant is not guaranteed and cannot be replaced by a full-data constant. Its presentation emphasizes the missing clean strong-convexity assumption rather than the proof's specific invalid use of full-loss curvature.
gold_decisions.shared_mathematical_weakness: The proof needs a positive curvature/secant bound for the clean aggregate, but curvature of the full weighted loss does not automatically provide that clean-only bound; an explicit clean strong-convexity condition and clean-defined lambda are required.
gold_decisions.uncovered_gold_detail: No substantive gold concern is left unrecognised; the prediction uses a different presentation, diagnosing the missing clean aggregate assumption rather than reproducing the exact full-versus-clean coefficient calculation.

component_coverage.gold_component: Using curvature of the full weighted loss as if it lower-bounded the clean-only radial inner product.
component_coverage.recognition_explanation: The prediction states that the clean aggregate may lack the positive curvature constant used in the proof, that the full-data constant cannot simply be substituted, and that lambda must be defined from the weighted clean aggregate.

gold_decisions.identity_explanation: Both identify the omitted clean-sample optimum-gradient variance term in the main residual and give the same type of noiseless counterexample and repair.
gold_decisions.shared_mathematical_weakness: The noisy residual omits the good-sample optimum-gradient-square contribution, making its right-hand side incorrectly vanish when clean individual gradients remain nonzero.

gold_decisions.identity_explanation: Both distinguish an ordering of one-step upper bounds at a common point from ordering the actual expected errors, and both reject the advertised actual-performance guarantee.
gold_decisions.shared_mathematical_weakness: A comparison of formal upper bounds does not imply ordering of the two algorithms' actual expected distances or trajectories.

component_coverage.gold_component: Invalid inference from same-point residual upper-bound ordering to actual expected-performance dominance.
component_coverage.recognition_explanation: The prediction directly states that the corollary compares upper bounds rather than actual expectations, gives a reversal example, and limits the repair to upper-bound ordering.

gold_decisions.identity_explanation: The gold entry bundles two independently diagnosable defects: the signed outlier residual cannot be ordered by coefficient comparison, and in the outlier-majority regime some outlier probabilities exceed 1/n. ISSUE-022 independently diagnoses the signed-residual defect, while ISSUE-021 independently diagnoses the probability-domination defect.
gold_decisions.shared_mathematical_weakness: The residual comparison is invalid because coefficient changes cannot be ordered without both sign control for the outlier excess and the claimed probability domination; the selected entries jointly cover both independent failures.
gold_decisions.uncovered_gold_detail: No substantive gold concern is left unrecognised; the two selected predictions separate the signed-sum failure from the outlier-majority probability failure.
gold_decisions.combination_explanation: The gold entry contains two distinct defects: (1) signed outlier excess terms can be negative, so lowering outlier probabilities does not preserve the required inequality; ISSUE-022 gives a self-contained diagnosis and counterexample. (2) when clean samples are fewer than half, some outlier probabilities exceed 1/n, invalidating the uniform-probability upper bound; ISSUE-021 gives a self-contained diagnosis and counterexample. Both are necessary to cover the full gold concern.

component_coverage.gold_component: Signed outlier residual terms may be negative, so replacing their probabilities by 1/n reverses the needed inequality.
component_coverage.recognition_explanation: ISSUE-022 explicitly identifies the negative outlier contribution, explains the reversed inequality, supplies a downweighted-outlier counterexample, and requires sign control or direct signed-sum comparison.

component_coverage.gold_component: In the outlier-majority regime, some outlier probabilities exceed 1/n, so the uniform-probability bound on nonnegative outlier gradient-square terms is invalid.
component_coverage.recognition_explanation: ISSUE-021 directly identifies outlier probabilities above 1/n when the good set is a minority, shows why the gradient-square terms cannot be bounded uniformly, and proposes the required probability or structural restriction.

gold_decisions.identity_explanation: Both identify that the proof uses without-replacement probabilities although the analyzed algorithm samples with replacement, propagating the wrong coefficients into the proof.
gold_decisions.shared_mathematical_weakness: The corollary proof analyzes a different sampling law from the declared with-replacement algorithm, so its probability coefficients and subsequent bounds do not establish the stated result.

component_coverage.gold_component: Use of without-replacement sampling probabilities in a proof for the with-replacement algorithm.
component_coverage.recognition_explanation: The prediction states both probability laws, notes the changed worst-ranked probability, explains that the wrong coefficients enter subsequent comparisons, and gives the corrected with-replacement repair.
